findings.title: Password verification can be bypassed when logging in with a backup code
findings.body: In the credentials `authorize()` handler, the user's password is only verified when `credentials.totpCode` is falsy (`if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`). The new backup-code branch (`if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)`) runs after this check and never validates `totpCode`. So a request that includes any non-empty `totpCode` (e.g. "1") together with a valid `backupCode` skips password verification entirely and authenticates successfully. The intended design (and the UI, which keeps the password field filled in the backup-code flow) is that a backup code is used together with the password; a crafted request defeats that. The backup-code branch should be gated on the password having been verified, or the password check should not depend on `totpCode` being empty when a backupCode is supplied.

findings.title: Existing 2FA users can never obtain backup codes, but the UI tells them to generate them in settings
findings.body: The setup endpoint rejects any user with `twoFactorAlreadyEnabled` (line 42-44), and it is the only place backup codes are generated. All users who enabled 2FA before this PR have `backupCodes = null`. When such a user clicks "Lost access" at login (or in the disable modal) and submits a backup code, they get `missing_backup_codes` — "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." — but there is no settings flow that generates codes for an already-enabled account. These users are permanently locked out of the backup-code recovery path with an error message pointing to a nonexistent feature. Either the setup endpoint needs to allow regenerating backup codes for enabled accounts (after password + TOTP verification), or the message must not instruct users to do something impossible.

findings.title: Closing the backup-codes dialog via onOpenChange/ESC skips onEnable and resetState
findings.body: After 2FA is enabled, the modal advances to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes`, and `onEnable()` plus `resetState()` are only invoked from the explicit "Close" button (`data-testid="backup-codes-close"`). If the user dismisses the dialog through `onOpenChange` (the dialog's X / ESC / outside-click path), neither callback runs: the parent's `onEnable` handler never fires so the settings switch state will not reflect that 2FA is now enabled, and the component's internal `step` stays on `DisplayBackupCodes`, so reopening the modal shows the stale backup-codes screen instead of the password step (while the server now rejects a new setup with TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled). The `onOpenChange` handler on the Dialog should also route through resetState/onEnable (distinguishing the already-enabled case).

findings.title: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, allowing single-use codes to be reused
findings.body: When a backup code is used, the code decrypts the stored array, finds the matching index, sets it to `null`, and writes the re-encrypted array back with `prisma.user.update`. Two concurrent login requests using the same code can both read the original array, both find the code at the same index, and both succeed before either write lands — the single-use guarantee ("Each backup code can be used exactly once") is broken under a race. The verification and consumption should be atomic (e.g. a transactional update or a compare-and-swap on the encrypted value).

findings.title: "Missing backup codes" never fires once all codes are used; users get a misleading "incorrect code" error
findings.body: Used backup codes are replaced with `null` inside the stored array rather than removing them or clearing the column. After all 10 codes are consumed, `user.backupCodes` is the string `"[null,null,...]"`, which is truthy, so the `if (!user.backupCodes) throw MissingBackupCodes` check never triggers; `indexOf` then returns -1 and the user sees "Backup code is incorrect." A user who has exhausted all codes is told their code is wrong instead of being told they have no backup codes left, leaving them without any indication of the actual state. The same pattern exists in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` line 54.

findings.title: No tests for the core feature: logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code
findings.body: The PR's headline functionality is using backup codes during login ("Lost access" flow) and the disable modal, but the only test coverage added is for the backup-codes display screen (download filename, copy toast, close button). The e2e file itself carries a TODO acknowledging this: "add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup". The single-use semantics, incorrect-code error paths, and the MissingBackupCodes path (existing 2FA users with null codes) are all untested, and the PR checklist confirms no tests proving the feature works. At minimum one e2e test should log in with a stored backup code and verify the code cannot be reused.
